tags.name: Profiles
tags.description:
A Profile is a configuration for the DAST scanning feature.

It includes various parameters such as authentication details, environment settings, a schema...
Profiles allow you to start scans on an endpoint and will keep track of the scan history.
This ensures consistency in repeated scans and helps track changes or improvements over time.

See [our documentation](https://docs.escape.tech/documentation/#profile) for more details.

tags.name: Assets
tags.description:
Manage every discovered Assets.

The public API provide basic CRUDs operations for all available assets.

See [our documentation](https://docs.escape.tech/documentation/asm/asset-management/) for more details.

tags.name: Integrations
tags.description:
Manage 3rd party integrations.

The public API provide basic CRUDs operations for all available integrations.

See [our documentation](https://https://docs.escape.tech/documentation/asm/integrations/) for more details.

tags.name: Workflows
tags.description:
Workflows Management

The public API provides CRUDs operations to manage workflows.

tags.name: Views
tags.description:
Saved views

The public API provides CRUDs operations to manage saved views and list the issues matching an issue view.

tags.name: Scans
tags.description:
A Scan is a run of the DAST or ASM scanning feature on an profile (DAST/ASM).

With the public API, you can trigger scans, track their status, and retrieve their results.

See [our documentation](https://docs.escape.tech/documentation/dast/) for more details.

tags.name: Retests
tags.description:
A Retest is a scan that re-validates selected issues on a DAST or AI pentest profile.

Start a retest with explicit issue IDs or a filter, then poll status, progress, and per-issue agents (status and outcome). The retest id is the scan id.

See [our documentation](https://docs.escape.tech/documentation/automate/public-api/) for more details.

tags.name: Emails
tags.description:
Read scan inbox emails.

The public API provides endpoints to list inbox emails and read their raw content without exposing storage links.

tags.name: Issues
tags.description:
Manage issues.

Identify, prioritize, and remediate the security issues and sensitive data exposures uncovered during ASM and DAST scanning

See [our documentation](https://docs.escape.tech/documentation/governance/vulnerability-management/) for more details.

tags.name: SecurityTests
tags.description:
Manage security tests.

Browse the security tests Escape can run, with their organization configuration (enabled state and custom severity), scanner and asset applicability, description and compliance mappings. Enable or disable security tests for your organization and override the severity assigned to their issues.

tags.name: Jobs
tags.description:
Asynchronous jobs.

Trigger export jobs and poll for completion and artefacts.

tags.name: KnowledgeFiles
tags.description:
Manage organization knowledge files.

The knowledge file library gives AI pentests context about your organization. Upload files with a signed URL, list them, and delete them.

tags.name: Events
tags.description:
Manage events.

The public API provides basic CRUDs operations to manage events.

tags.name: Tags
tags.description:
Manage tags.

The public API provides basic CRUDs operations to manage tags.

tags.name: CustomRules
tags.description:
Manage your custom rules.

The public API provides basic CRUDs operations to manage custom rules.

See [our documentation](https://docs.escape.tech/documentation/dast/custom-rules/) for more details.

tags.name: Upload
tags.description:
Upload helper for Escape Platform.

The public API provides endpoints to upload files to the platform.

tags.name: Locations
tags.description:
A Location is a proxy environment through which Escape sends requests.

The public API provide basic CRUDs operations for your private locations.

See [our documentation](https://docs.escape.tech/documentation/tooling/private-location/) for more details.

tags.name: Audit
tags.description:
List audit logs.

The public API provides endpoints to list audit logs.

See [our documentation](https://docs.escape.tech/documentation/enterprise/audit-logs/) for more details.

tags.name: Projects
tags.description:
Projects Management

The public API provides CRUDs operations to manage projects.

tags.name: RegressionTests
tags.description:
Manage regression tests.

Create regression tests from a source report, run them, and track their history. A regression test re-validates a finding against an updated codebase.

tags.name: Roles
tags.description:
Roles Management

The public API provides CRUDs operations to manage roles.

tags.name: Users
tags.description:
Users Management

The public API provides CRUDs operations to manage users.

tags.name: Statistics
tags.description:
Organization Statistics

High-level organization security posture statistics.

tags.name: Asm
tags.description:
Attack Surface Management

Trigger and manage ASM discovery scans on your attack surface.

See [our documentation](https://docs.escape.tech/documentation/asm/) for more details.

tags.name: Compliance
tags.description:
Compliance frameworks

Read compliance posture at organization, application, and scan level, and manage enabled compliance frameworks.

tags.name: OrganizationSettings
tags.description:
Organization settings.

Manage organization-wide settings: issue SLA policy, AI system prompt, project propagation and scoped webhook export. Scan kill switches are read-only.

tags.name: AIChats
tags.description:
Copilot chats.

Create, list and resume Copilot chats. Only the chats owned by the authenticated user are exposed.

tags.name: Beta
tags.description:
Beta

These endpoints are in beta and are subject to change.

tags.name: Validations
tags.description:
Target validations.

Start a validation to check that a target (asset) is reachable and in scope, then poll for status and output.

tags.name: VaultVariables
tags.description:
Manage vault variables.

Vault variables are secret references used by scan authentication configs. Values are write-only: they are accepted on create and update, but never returned by the API.

info.title: Escape Public API
info.description:
This API enables you to operate [Escape](https://escape.tech/) programmatically.

All requests must be authenticated with a valid API key, provided in the `X-ESCAPE-API-KEY` header.
For example: `X-ESCAPE-API-KEY: YOUR_API_KEY`.

You can find your API key in the [Escape dashboard](https://app.escape.tech/user/).

On update, use [PUT /profiles/:profileId](#tag/profiles/PUT/profiles/:profileId) with this field.

mode.description: Scan aggressiveness. `read_only` runs non-destructive tests and avoids state-changing operations (preferred for production targets). `read_write` runs exhaustive tests including mutations (use on pre-production, staging, or dedicated test environments). If omitted, the API uses `mode` from the configuration JSON when present; otherwise the profile defaults to `read_only`. When both this field and a nested `mode` exist, this top-level value wins.

post.description:
Create a schema asset.

The schema data can either be fetched from a URL, uploaded from a file, or sent inline as raw
content.

**Fetch example:**
```json
{
  "asset_type": "SCHEMA",
  "fetch": {
    "url": "https://api.example.com/v1"
  }
}
```

**Upload example:**

The file should first be uploaded to the Escape Platform using the [upload endpoint](/v3/#tag/upload/post/upload/signed-url).

The upload endpoint returns an `id` that should be used in the `temporaryObjectKey` field.

```json
{
  "asset_type": "SCHEMA",
  "upload": {
    "temporaryObjectKey": "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"
  }
}
```

**Inline content example:**

Send the raw schema content directly (at most 2 MB) when the caller cannot PUT to the pre-signed
upload URL. The content is stored and converted with the same BUILD_SCHEMA workflow. The response
is the created schema asset; its `id` is the `schemaId` used to attach the schema to a profile.

```json
{
  "asset_type": "SCHEMA",
  "content": "{ \"openapi\": \"3.0.0\", ... }",
  "contentType": "application/json",
  "filename": "schema.json"
}
```

post.description:
Add a file to the organization knowledge library. Files are used as context by AI pentests.

This is a two-step flow:

1. Create a signed upload URL with `POST /v3/upload/signed-url`.
2. `PUT` the file content to the returned `url`.
3. Call this endpoint with the returned `id` as `temporaryObjectKey`.

The file is processed asynchronously: poll the list endpoint until the status is `COMPLETED` or `FAILED`.

Each upload is stored under its own object, so uploading a file with an already used name adds a new file instead of overwriting the previous one. Uploads are limited to 35MB.

post.description:
Retrieve a signed URL link to upload a file to the Escape Platform.

By running a query with this endpoint, you will receive a signed URL that you can use to upload a file to the Escape Platform.

```json
{
  "url": "[SIGNED URL]",
  "id": "[SIGNED URL ID]"
}
```

With the url, you are able to upload one file:

```bash
curl -X PUT --data-binary '@./schema.json' "[SIGNED URL]"
```

Now, you are able to use the previously received id in another query.
For example to update a schema of your application.

Optionally pass `contentType` and `filename` query parameters so the uploaded object keeps its
MIME type and original name:

```bash
curl -X POST "/v3/upload/signed-url?contentType=application/json&filename=schema.har"
```

When `contentType` is provided it is part of the signed request, so the `PUT` must send the same
`Content-Type` header:

```bash
curl -X PUT -H "Content-Type: application/json" --data-binary '@./schema.json' "[SIGNED URL]"
```

open.description: Issues first seen at or before the bucket start that were still open at the bucket end

resolved.description: Cumulative count of issues first seen at or before the bucket start that were already resolved as of the bucket end. Once an issue is resolved it is counted in every later bucket, so this value repeats; difference consecutive buckets to get resolutions per bucket.

openResolved.description: Time series of open vs resolved issue counts

x.description: Time bucket start date (ISO 8601). The bucket covers [x, x + interval), except the final bucket, which ends at `end`.

y.description: Average API health score for the bucket, weighting each application equally. Each application contributes its last known finished-scan score, which is carried forward for buckets after its most recent scan, so a value can repeat across buckets; null when no application has scan data for the bucket.

averageApiHealth.description: Time series of average API health scores
